name: Acne
tagline: Treatable. Don't pick. See a doctor for severe.

what_is_it.heading: Acne in plain terms
what_is_it.lede: Acne is what happens when oil and dead skin cells block pores. Sometimes the blocked pore becomes inflamed by normal skin bacteria — that's when you get the red, sore spots. It is not caused by being dirty.
paragraphs: Acne is most common in teenagers because hormonal changes increase oil production. But adults get it too — especially women in their 20s and 30s, often along the jawline. About 85% of South Africans will have acne at some point.

Mild acne usually responds to over-the-counter treatments and good skin habits. Moderate to severe acne — especially with cysts, scarring, or pain — needs a doctor. Effective prescription treatments exist. Untreated severe acne can leave permanent scars and affect self-esteem for years.

items.body: Of South Africans get acne at some point. It is one of the most common skin conditions in the world.

items.headline: Treatable
items.body: Even severe acne responds to modern treatment. The earlier you start, the less scarring you'll have to live with.

items.headline: Don't pick
items.body: Picking, squeezing, and harsh scrubbing make acne worse and cause permanent scars. Hardest habit to break — and the most important.

items.headline: Not your fault
items.body: Acne is not caused by being dirty, eating chocolate, or anything you did. It is mostly hormones and genetics.

pull_quote.text: The single most powerful step in treating acne is starting early — before the scarring sets in. If over-the-counter treatments aren't working after 8 weeks, see a doctor.

signs.heading: Types of acne — and how serious
signs.lede: Acne ranges from a few spots to deep, painful cysts. The type matters because it changes the treatment.

items.title: Mild — blackheads and whiteheads
items.description: Small bumps without much inflammation. Usually responds to good skincare and over-the-counter products. Try benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid first.

items.title: Moderate — red, inflamed spots
items.description: Red papules and pustules across face, chest, back. Try over-the-counter treatment for 8 weeks. If no improvement — see a doctor. Prescription options work better.

items.title: Severe — cysts and scarring
items.description: Deep, painful lumps that linger for weeks. Leaves scars. See a doctor as soon as possible. Isotretinoin (Roaccutane) is highly effective for this.

myths.heading: What is true and what is not

items.myth: Chocolate, oily food, and sugar cause acne.
items.fact: The evidence is weak and varies between people. High-sugar/high-dairy diets may worsen acne in some, but they don't cause it. Hormones and genetics matter much more.

items.myth: Wash your face more — that'll clear it up.
items.fact: Over-washing dries and irritates skin, making acne worse. Gentle cleanser twice a day is enough. Harsh scrubs inflame the skin and worsen redness.

items.myth: Toothpaste, lemon juice, and bicarb work as home treatments.
items.fact: All can irritate or burn the skin and worsen scarring. Use proper acne products — benzoyl peroxide, salicylic acid, retinoids — designed to work safely.
Tanning can dry out skin temporarily, making spots less visible. Long term, sun damage worsens scarring and ages your skin. Treat the acne — protect your skin.

prevention.heading: Daily habits that help
prevention.lede: You can't fully prevent acne — but you can reduce flare-ups, support treatment, and prevent scars.

items.title: Gentle cleanser twice a day
items.description: Morning and evening — water-based, fragrance-free. Don't scrub. Don't use bar soap or harsh scrubs on acne-prone skin.

items.title: Non-comedogenic SPF every day
items.description: Sun protection matters even with acne. Look for 'non-comedogenic' (won't block pores) on the label. Most major brands have these.

items.title: Don't pick — don't squeeze
items.description: Picking pushes infection deeper and turns spots into scars. The mark from a picked spot can last 6 months. The mark from a left-alone spot — maybe 2 weeks.

items.title: Give treatments 8 weeks
items.description: Acne treatments take 6–12 weeks to show full effect. Don't switch every few days. Stick with one approach and judge by the 8-week mark.

items.title: Start with over-the-counter for mild acne
items.description: Benzoyl peroxide 2.5% gel or salicylic acid wash. Use once a day for a week, then twice if tolerated. Available at any pharmacy without prescription.

items.title: If no improvement after 8 weeks — see a doctor
items.description: Free at any government clinic. Prescription topical retinoids and antibiotics work much better than OTC for moderate acne.

items.title: If severe or scarring — see soon
items.description: Severe cystic acne can leave permanent scars. Treatments like isotretinoin (Roaccutane) are highly effective. Government clinics can refer to a dermatologist.

items.title: Treat the whole area, not just the spots
items.description: Apply treatments thinly across the affected area — not just on individual spots. Prevents the next breakout instead of catching up.

items.title: Protect your skin from the sun
items.description: Acne treatments make skin sun-sensitive. Use non-comedogenic SPF 30+ daily. Sun also worsens dark marks left by past spots.

get_help.heading: Where to go
get_help.lede: Most acne can be treated at home or at a primary care clinic. Severe acne benefits from dermatology referral — available through the public system.
